title: Critical Limit Experiment for Fused Current-Status and Right-Censored Samples
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded the sound Gaussian–Poisson equivalence incremental below the field floor: paper_score_ceiling 6.4 < 7.4; salvageable=false. The abstract interval optimizer and unspecified comparison kernels lack a computable value or implementable procedure.
gap_reasons: The claimed attaining critical-regime interval is only an abstract weak-star cluster kernel, and the finite-sample intervals depend on unspecified comparison kernels; neither L_kappa(0.1) nor an implementable approximation to its optimizer is supplied.

The theorem-level positioning is otherwise specific, but the cited bibliography includes RaySchmidtHieber2018 and Donoho1994 without a relevance/comparison sentence; add their precise relation to the Gaussian--Poisson experiment and interval-value claims, or remove them if they are not relied upon.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 derived uniform two-way Gaussian–Poisson equivalence over the supported C1 tangent class, including the censoring-atom compensator, exact contrast range, decision-value transfer, and analytic randomized interval attainment. The math panel passed, but D0.5 graded the sound result incremental below the field floor because the optimizer and finite-sample transfer do not provide a computable value or implementable interval procedure. A future re-raise needs a genuinely constructive decision rule with verified approximation and calibration, plus the bibliographic positioning repair.
tldr: At an interior target satisfying \(t_0>L>0\), two independent sources observe one finite-stratum event law through current-status and right-censoring mechanisms. At \(m n^{-1/3}\to\kappa\), the survey contributes Gaussian white noise and the rare cohort contributes a finite censoring-thinned Poisson failure process, including the deterministic likelihood compensator from a target-time censoring atom. Uniform two-way equivalence holds over the full supported \(C^1\) density-slack class. Its exact local contrast range is \([ -S,S]\), where \(S=\sum_z|w_z|L\min\{f_z^0(t_0)-\eta,\eta^{-1}-f_z^0(t_0)\}\); these bounds are infimum and supremum values and need not be attained by tangents. Exact local squared-risk and uniformly 90 percent-honest connected-interval values transfer, an optimal randomized limit interval exists on this compact action range, and forward transport plus explicit coverage repair attains the limit value in the finite experiments.
gap: Tang, Banerjee, and Kosorok establish an \(n^{-1/3}\) inspection-grid/isotonic boundary law and adaptive current-status inference, not a continuous-inspection experiment equivalence. Existing mixed-censor efficiency theory assumes a nonvanishing right-censored source fraction, while existing equivalence results treat Gaussian and Poisson observation models separately. No checked result gives both deficiencies for the critical rare-cohort mixed-censor experiment or retains the censoring-atom normalization term.
fill: The full experiment theorem supplies uniform forward and reverse kernels, the atom-sensitive product likelihood, bounded-loss decision transfer, and a concrete route to a shortest honest critical-regime interval.
